Field notes · Session planning

What to wear for family photos

A simple approach to colors, texture, and feeling like yourselves.

The best outfit is one you can move in and recognize yourself wearing. Start with the setting and the season, then build a small palette that gives everyone room to look like themselves.

Choose a palette, not a uniform.

Pick two or three related colors and add neutrals. Cream, soft blue, and muted green can sit comfortably together outdoors. Warm brown, ivory, and denim are another easy starting point. You don’t need every person in the same shirt.

Mix texture with quiet patterns.

Knitwear, linen, cotton, and a little layering add variety without fighting for attention. One subtle pattern can work beautifully; several bold patterns together can pull your eye away from faces. Lay the outfits beside each other before deciding.

Let comfort do some of the work.

Choose clothes that fit well while sitting, walking, and picking up a child. Have everyone try on the full outfit, including shoes. Bring practical walking shoes if the location involves a trail, even if you change before the photographs.

Plan for little people.

Children are more comfortable in familiar clothes than in something stiff or itchy. Bring an extra layer, a small snack, and a backup outfit when it makes sense. A relaxed child matters more than a perfectly tucked shirt.

Try this: take a quick phone photo of all the outfits laid out together. If one item dominates the whole picture, simplify that piece.

Keep the location in mind.

For a green outdoor setting, a little contrast helps the family stand out. Against stone or architecture, softer colors and texture can keep the image from feeling too busy. We’ll talk about your location and the light before your session.
